newsitem.title: USA: Owens Corning to appeal Florida ruling.
newsitem.headline: Owens Corning to appeal Florida ruling.

text.p: A spokesman for Owens Corning said Thursday the company would appeal a Palm Beach County jury's order that it pay $31 million to an Ohio man who is dying of cancer linked to asbestos.

"The verdict, particularly the punitive damage verdict, is wildly unjustified and unreasonable. We will vigorously appeal that," said Bill Hamilton, spokesman for the Toledo, Ohio-based company. "We've had outrageous verdicts like this in the past. They are always reduced."

Hamilton said Owens Corning believes the ruling, which was handed down late Tuesday, violates Florida law, which limits punitive damages. Electrical worker Deward Ballard, 59, was also awarded $1.8 million in compensatory damages.
He also has settled a similar suit against W.R. Grace of Boca Raton.

Ballard was exposed to asbestos while working at an oil refinery in Houston from 1962 to 1963. Thirty-two years later, a chest X-ray showed Ballard had mesothelioma, a rare cancer linked to asbestos exposure.

Hamilton noted Owens Corning has not made the product Ballard was exposed to for 25 years. And noting the $1.5 billion in asbestos-linked payments the company has made already and another $1.4 billion it has in reserve, he said: "The purpose of punitive damages is to punish and deter. We've certainly been punished as a company, substantially, already."
